claim:
The exclusion rests on absence where opportunity is frequent: independent each before a finite verb is over a hundred times as frequent as every in COCA, and across nearly eight hundred COCA and NOW lines with every before a verb it never stands as an ordinary fused head. Where it does stand without a noun, the noun is recoverable from a coordinate or the preceding turn, or every closes a binomial.\footnote{COCA List counts (17 September 2026): each has 1,578, each was 1,005, each will 507, against every will 12, every has 8, every was 3; of 618 COCA lines for every before a verb and 164 NOW lines for every was and every has, none shows the fused-head use. The residue is ellipsis (if not every, then almost every male head of household, Social History, 1995) and binomials (to be open and generous to all and every, fiction, 2015). The screened lines are under corpus/exclusion\_tests/, and the check is tabled in the quantifier supplement.}

claim: Fusion is held fixed for adjectives (\mention{the rich}) in all four implementations. \textit{CGEL} (I3) uses it a second time, for independent determinatives, and pays for that use with one condition on the fused inner phrase (nine cells) and with rules stated once for NPs and again for DPs (twelve cells, four rules). The two ordinary-Head implementations remove the second use and share the saving; they buy it differently. D-noun (I1) moves the determinatives one node down the taxonomy and keeps the head condition as it is. Separate D with ordinary Head (I2) keeps D a primary category and adds a disjunct to the head condition, and the Dn column records the 32 derivations that go through that disjunct.
